objective: Determine whether the sqrt3 x sqrt3 three-sublattice order of Guo et al. is reachable on a 49-atom triangular patch, using the per-shot sublattice order parameter <|m|> as the discriminator.

paper.title: Order-by-disorder and emergent Kosterlitz-Thouless phase in a triangular Rydberg array

observable.description: <|m|> — modulus of the per-shot three-sublattice order parameter m = (3/N) sum_j (n_j - nbar) exp(i K.r_j), averaged over shots

open_questions.question: 1.0 is the algebraic maximum of <|m|>, not a prediction. <|m|> already reads 0.18 on a *disordered* 49-atom array — what value should count as having observed order?
open_questions.why: no finite-size prediction for this geometry was available when the spec was written
open_questions.impact: no step reads this number; it only matters to whoever judges the result, and a ceiling that cannot be reached makes any measured order look weak

open_questions.question: L = 7 (N = 49) is what a FRESNEL_CAN1-class device fits; Guo et al. work at larger N. Is 49 enough for the order to separate from the finite-size floor?
open_questions.why: L = 10 reaches ~41 um and needs an SA1-class device
open_questions.impact: if not, the whole scan measures the floor and the experiment cannot answer the objective

_notes: R_b/a sets the phase, not a paper value copied across: at Omega = 2*pi*2 MHz and the FRESNEL_CAN1-class C6, R_b = 6.4 um, so a = 5.3 um gives R_b/a = 1.21 — an atom blockades its six nearest neighbours but not the next-nearest, which is what selects the sqrt3 x sqrt3 three-sublattice order. Guo et al. quote R_b ~ 1.2a. a = 5.3 um also clears the 5 um minimum trap spacing. tau_ns stops at 5800 because the two 100 ns amplitude edges plus tau must fit the 6000 ns maximum sequence duration. N = 49 (L = 7) is the FRESNEL_CAN1-class variant; L = 10 (N = 100) reaches ~41 um and needs SA1 — see README.md. The register was sized against Pulser's bundled AnalogDevice as a stand-in, not against live device specs, so validate-emu will reject it if the live device is tighter.
